papers.title: Hidden Drowsiness in Wakefulness: Differences in Resting-State EEG Profiles in Natural Short Sleepers Versus Recommended Length Sleepers.
papers.summary: Compared resting-state eyes-open EEG in natural short sleepers (≤6 h/night without subjective daytime dysfunction) versus recommended-length sleepers, finding higher global alpha power and regionally steeper aperiodic exponents (especially occipital) in short sleepers, with a trend toward increasing exponents over time. These markers suggest increased drowsiness and less stable wakefulness under low stimulation, possibly masked by perceived resilience to short sleep.

papers.title: Targeting memory consolidation in major depression via pharmacological slow-wave sleep promotion
papers.summary: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial in 22 MDD patients and 20 matched controls tested single nocturnal doses of GHB and trazodone with polysomnography and pre/post-sleep memory testing. GHB strongly increased slow-wave sleep duration and delta power, but neither drug improved declarative, procedural, or emotional memory consolidation, challenging the assumption that increasing SWS alone improves overnight memory.

papers.title: MLE EEG Toolbox: A Personal AI Laboratory Assistant for Literature-Informed and Reproducible M/EEG Research
papers.summary: The authors present MLE EEG Toolbox, a locally deployed AI framework integrating natural-language-guided M/EEG analysis, literature retrieval, validated operation selection, and computational provenance for reproducibility. It achieved action-selection accuracies of 85.6% for EEG and 95.5% for MEG, with 142 cross-platform tests showing close numerical agreement and demonstrated spectral, network, decoding, and source analyses on public datasets.

papers.title: A Soft Sponge-Pillar Electrode Platform for Motion-Tolerant Ambulatory EEG and Sleep Monitoring.
papers.summary: Developed a soft carbon black–PDMS sponge-pillar EEG electrode, fabricated by sugar templating, that bypasses hair with a firm base and uses a porous conductive-gel-loaded tip for low-modulus, high-area scalp contact. It achieved 1.62×10^4 Ω contact impedance at 10 Hz with gel stability over 18 h and recorded EEG during motion (headbands, headphones, caps) at 16.46 dB SNR.

papers.title: Protocol-aware dual-view single-channel EEG sleep staging with improved N1 discrimination on public sleep-EDF and SHHS benchmarks.
papers.summary: Developed DualViewSeqSleepNet, a protocol-aware single-channel EEG sleep staging model combining raw-waveform and spectral encoders with cross-epoch aggregation and N1-aware auxiliary loss. On Sleep-EDF it reached macro-F1 0.821, accuracy 0.869, and kappa 0.808, improving N1 F1 from 0.506 to 0.535; on SHHS-1 it achieved macro-F1 0.791 and accuracy 0.854 without retuning.

papers.title: Circadian feeding rhythm loss drives sex-specific β-cell dysfunction in diet-induced obesity.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Exposed male and female C57BL/6 mice to high-fat diet for eight weeks and assessed circadian feeding/activity, glucose tolerance, insulin secretion, islet RNA-seq and ATAC-seq, testing time-restricted feeding. DIO disrupted circadian fasting/feeding and abolished circadian glucose tolerance and GSIS in males but not females, reduced circadian-regulated islet transcripts by 42.1%, and dark-phase tRF restored circadian glucose tolerance, GSIS and islet gene expression.

papers.title: Actimetry-Derived Sleep and Circadian Parameters in a Population-Based Sample from São Paulo: Findings from the EPISONO Cohort.
papers.summary: Derived actimetry-based sleep, circadian, light exposure, and skin temperature parameters from 404 EPISONO cohort participants in São Paulo to establish urban reference values and model demographic and lifestyle effects. Older age, female sex, lower socioeconomic status, obesity, and season were associated with distinct differences in sleep timing, rhythm stability, fragmentation, and light exposure.

papers.title: Spikes in the night: rapid eye movement sleep maximally attenuates epileptiform spike morphology.
papers.summary: Quantified nine morphological features of 7379 interictal epileptiform discharges across sleep-wake states in 17 adults with focal epilepsy using continuous video-EEG telemetry. REM IEDs showed the shallowest slopes, bluntest peaks, and smallest amplitudes/area, while awake IEDs were steepest and spikiest, indicating maximal attenuation of epileptiform morphology in REM.

papers.title: NeuroSim: a clinically informed multi-disorder EEG simulator with personalized pattern injection and AI-driven neurological modeling
papers.summary: Presented NeuroSim, a clinically informed simulator generating synthetic multichannel EEG with user-controlled, region- and severity-specific disease pattern injection across AD, PD, schizophrenia, epilepsy and FTD. A convolutional-attention classifier trained on simulated data reached 95.3–96.8% hold-out accuracy, and augmenting real clinical EEG with NeuroSim samples raised AD-vs-control accuracy from 91.6% to 94.5% and PD-vs-control from 90.9% to 94.0%.

papers.title: Dopamine dynamics in a mouse model of temporal lobe seizures with impaired consciousness.
papers.summary: Used fiber photometry and calcium imaging in awake head-fixed mice with hippocampal-stimulation-induced focal limbic seizures to examine cortical and ventral tegmental area dopamine dynamics alongside behavioral responsiveness. Seizures produced sustained increases in cortical and VTA dopamine but reduced transient task-evoked dopamine and behavioral responses, suggesting dysregulation across time scales that may resemble delirium/encephalopathy.

papers.title: Seizure Prediction Using Channel-Optimized Intracranial EEG With Variable Interictal and Preictal Durations.
papers.journal: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
papers.summary: Evaluated seizure prediction on intracranial EEG using six combinations of interictal (24 h, 48 h) and preictal (30, 60, 90 min) durations and three classification strategies including channel-optimization-based majority voting. On the SWEC-ETHZ dataset the method reached up to 87.7% sensitivity, 94.6% specificity, 0.912 AUC at segment level and 95.9% sensitivity with 0.05/h FPR at event level, with channel optimization outperforming all-channel and single-channel strategies.

papers.title: AI-Based Monitoring Devices for the Identification of Circadian Parameters as Digital Predictive Biomarkers of Neurodegenerative Diseases in Older Adults: Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-2020 systematic review synthesized 13 records (10 eligible studies, 2015-2025) on AI-enhanced wearable and objective sensing of circadian parameters as digital predictive biomarkers in older and cognitively vulnerable adults, mostly wrist actigraphy, with heterogeneous endpoints precluding meta-analysis. Circadian fragmentation was associated with functional decline, dementia risk, and cognitive performance, but no AI model was externally validated; certainty was moderate for actigraphy-fragmentation associations in institutional settings and low for community predictive biomarker claims, and a 4-layer reference architecture with a layered validation pathway was proposed.

papers.title: Effects of Environmental Enrichment on the Behavior of Scarlet Macaws (Ara macao cyanopterus) for Reintroduction.
papers.summary: Evaluated environmental enrichment effects on behaviors relevant to wild survival and on abnormal behaviors in hand-reared scarlet macaws in the pre-release phase, comparing pre-enrichment and enrichment phases with Wilcoxon tests and association indices. Enrichment significantly increased exploration and group cohesion, decreased resting, self-care, and abnormal behaviors, and yielded more individuals with high release-suitability scores, without changing flight behavior.

papers.title: Effects of Circadian Disruption and Chronotype on Postural Stability During Quiet Stance.
papers.summary: Examined how circadian regularity, misalignment parameters (composite phase deviation, interdaily stability, intradaily variability), and chronotype relate to postural stability during quiet stance in 39 healthy adults using force-platform center-of-pressure measures and recurrence quantification analysis. Greater circadian disruption and later chronotype were associated with greater postural instability, including increased sway and higher laminarity and trapping time.

papers.title: Frontal Low-Frequency Electroencephalographic Coherence in Bipolar Disorder: A Covariate-Controlled Secondary Analysis of a Public Resting-State EEG Feature Dataset.
papers.summary: Tested frontal/frontopolar low-frequency resting-state EEG coherence in bipolar disorder versus healthy controls, depressive disorder, and schizophrenia in a covariate-controlled secondary analysis of a public dataset (n=472). Bipolar disorder showed higher adjusted delta/theta coherence than all comparison groups (partial η2=.037-.040), with effects strongest in frontopolar pairs and attenuated when anterior electrodes were excluded.

papers.title: Dermal α-synuclein seeding in relation to REM sleep behavior disorder across prodromal and Parkinson disease cohorts.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional PPMI analysis of controls, polysomnography-confirmed RBD, and Parkinson disease participants, dermal α-synuclein seed amplification assay (SAA) positivity was found in 53.3% of RBD participants versus none of the controls, with faster amplification kinetics in RBD at both lysate dilutions. Within PD, SAA positivity was higher in the body/peripheral-enriched than brain/motor-enriched phenotype (83.3% vs 47.6%; p=0.067).

papers.title: A scoping review of sleep outcomes in congenital hydrocephalus.
papers.summary: A PRISMA-compliant scoping review of seven studies (1,116 participants) examining sleep in congenital hydrocephalus found reported increases in total sleep time and sleep apnea burden, greater fatigue versus normative values, and EEG abnormalities during sleep, with mixed sleep-related quality of life; small samples and inconsistent methods limited interpretation.

papers.title: Group-specific associations among sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and frontal alpha asymmetry in college students: evidence from a cross-sectional EEG study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional EEG study of 120 college students comparing 60 with elevated depressive symptoms to 60 controls, examining associations among sleep quality (PSQI), depressive symptoms, and frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA). The depressive-symptom group had worse PSQI scores and lower composite FAA, and FAA correlated with PSQI and depressive symptoms only in that group; a BMI-adjusted model explained R2=0.243.

papers.title: Integrated roles of regulatory non-coding RNAs in circadian gene expression and disease pathogenesis.
papers.summary: Reviews recent progress on microRNAs, long non-coding RNAs, and circular RNAs in circadian rhythm regulation and their dysfunction in pathological conditions including cancer, metabolic disorders, and neurological disease. Emphasizes an integrative cross-ncRNA-class view and context-specific gene regulation, noting circRNA mechanisms remain emerging.

papers.title: From snoring to obstructive sleep apnea: A narrative review of pathophysiology, clinical implications and multimodal management.
papers.summary: This narrative review reframes snoring as a clinically informative manifestation of upper airway dysfunction, applying the OSA endotypic model (collapsibility, muscle responsiveness, arousal threshold, loop gain) and proposing a pre-test probability-based, phenotype-driven diagnostic and multimodal management approach.

papers.title: Association between quantitative REM sleep without atonia and skeletal muscle indices by subsequent phenoconversion status in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.summary: In 114 patients with video-polysomnography-confirmed iRBD (88 non-converters, 26 converters), converters showed higher tonic, phasic, and total REM sleep without atonia indices, and total RWAI was inversely associated with skeletal muscle mass and fat-free mass indices only among converters (significant RWAI-by-phenoconversion interactions for SMI and FFMI).

papers.title: What's in a Story? Studying Neural Narrative Engagement with Auditory Passages Using EEG Inter-Subject Correlation
papers.summary: Using dense-array EEG inter-subject correlation (ISC) in 46 adults listening to social and non-social narrated literary excerpts, this study found no significant ISC differences for broad social/non-social categorizations, but ISC for high sociocognitive word usage exceeded medium and low usage in reliable component RC3. Summed interest, compulsion, and enjoyment ratings correlated positively with ISC for RC2 and across RC1-RC3, with passage content and behavioral responses contributing additively.

papers.title: Circadian Regulation of Gastrointestinal Physiology and Disease: Mechanisms, Chrononutrition, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
papers.summary: This narrative review integrates molecular clock mechanisms with clinical evidence on circadian regulation of gastrointestinal physiology and disease, covering chrononutrition and chronomodulated chemotherapy. It emphasizes that meal-timing effects on metabolic markers do not consistently exceed calorie restriction and that sleep-intervention trials have not established relapse prevention, highlighting the need for controlled trials assessing biological phase and disease activity.

papers.title: Clinical outcomes and EEG monitoring in absence epilepsy trials: A narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review of EEG monitoring in absence epilepsy trials reports that nearly 100% of clinical absence seizures show sustained generalized spike-and-wave discharges, that over 49% of electrographic seizures are asymptomatic, that cognitive and behavioral comorbidities are highly prevalent, and that antiseizure medications effective in absence epilepsy reduce GSW. It recommends incorporating ≥24-h EEG monitoring and comorbidity outcomes into future clinical trials.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation remodels hepatic immune microenvironment via circadian gene dysregulation and promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression.
papers.summary: Using GEO transcriptomic datasets, a rat sleep-deprivation model, machine learning, and immune-infiltration analyses, this study identified six core circadian rhythm-related genes (Cirbp, Srebf1, Fbxo31, Hsp90aa1, Btc, Dlgap1) mediating sleep deprivation-induced hepatic immune remodeling. Cirbp and Hsp90aa1 were associated with immune infiltration and prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma, and Serpine1 was independently identified as a key sleep deprivation-related gene.

papers.title: Nocturnal Sweating in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Systematic Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 10 studies and exploratory meta-analysis of three comparative studies found nocturnal sweating was not consistently associated with OSA severity indices; the pooled odds ratio for increased nocturnal sweating in OSA was non-significant (OR 1.85, 95% CI 0.87-3.92, I2=91.7%), though sweating may reflect hypoxemic burden and sympathetic activation and improved with PAP therapy.

papers.title: Rituximab-responsive epilepsia partialis continua in autoimmune Polyendocrine syndrome: A video-EEG-EMG polygraphic study.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: This case report describes a 54-year-old woman with Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome presenting with epilepsia partialis continua of the right III-V fingers, localized by ictal HMPAO-SPECT, FDG-PET, and video-EEG-EMG polygraphy showing left central spikes preceding EMG bursts by 30-40 ms. Corticosteroids improved symptoms but caused severe glycemic worsening and multiple subsequent therapies failed, whereas rituximab produced complete and sustained clinical and electrophysiological remission at 18-month follow-up.

papers.title: Metrics Reflecting Cumulative Exposure to Nocturnal Hypoxia Demonstrate Promising Performance in Distinguishing between Moderate and Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.summary: In 30 patients with moderate or severe OSA assessed by actigraphy and nocturnal oximetry, cumulative time with SpO2 below 90% and hypoxic burden remained independently associated with severe disease after BMI adjustment, with AUCs of 0.86 and 0.84 respectively, outperforming desaturation frequency (AUC 0.78).

papers.title: Depressive symptoms moderate daily anticipated and momentary emotion dynamics and associate with complex brain network topology: Resting-state EEG and ecological momentary assessment evidence.
papers.summary: Combining resting-state EEG with a 14-day ecological momentary assessment in 96 young adults, this study found that anticipated emotion prospectively predicted momentary positive emotion (β = .191) and inversely predicted negative emotion (β = -.125), with depressive symptoms moderating this link above PHQ-9 scores of roughly 5.7-9.7. Theta and delta band minimum spanning tree topology was indirectly associated with daily emotional dynamics via baseline depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Perioperative esketamine is associated with attenuated sleep deprivation-related cognitive dysfunction: a retrospective biomarker cohort study of the ferroptosis-neuroinflammation axis.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: In a retrospective biomarker cohort of 398 older adults undergoing major non-cardiac surgery, perioperative esketamine was associated with lower odds of early postoperative cognitive decline in sleep-deprived patients (adjusted OR 0.49) and with attenuation of a peripheral ferroptosis-related/inflammatory phenotype (lower 4-HNE, MDA, ACSL4, IL-6 and higher GSH, GPX4, SLC7A11). An exploratory redox score was independently associated with cognitive decline, with a model-based mediated proportion of 54%.

papers.title: Pain in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder: Findings from longitudinal and deep-phenotyping cohorts.
papers.summary: In NAPS Consortium cohorts, isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (n=507) was associated with higher odds of greater pain severity than controls (OR 2.24), and moderate-severe baseline pain predicted phenoconversion to overt synucleinopathy (HR 2.21). Cross-sectional striatal dopamine transporter binding was not associated with pain severity, and objective pressure algometry did not differ between groups.

papers.title: Exploring the genetic determinants of ALS in a North Indian cohort using a genomic screening approach
papers.summary: In 73 clinically diagnosed ALS patients from North India, targeted sequencing, repeat expansion analysis, and whole exome sequencing identified a pathogenic TARDBP variant, one C9orf72 expansion, pathogenic ATXN1 expansions, and rare variants in ANXA11, SIGMAR1, SETX, ERBB4, and NEK1. Poor sleep quality and excessive daytime sleepiness were frequent but not significantly associated with disease severity.

papers.title: The impact of mindfulness on sleep, cognitive function and athletic performance of young males migrating to the plateau.
papers.summary: In a randomized trial of 96 young male migrants to high altitude, 8 weeks of mindfulness-based cognitive therapy improved sleep quality (PSQI median 7.5 to 5) and cognitive processing speed (P300 latency 387 to 357 ms) versus controls, but 3000-m run time and grade improvement rates did not differ between groups.

papers.title: Association between sleep bruxism, awake bruxism, perceived stress and coping strategies among dental students: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional survey of 570 dental students, sleep bruxism prevalence was 57.4% and awake bruxism 39.5%; sleep bruxism was associated with higher perceived stress and greater emotion- and problem-focused coping, whereas awake bruxism was independently associated only with lower problem-focused coping.

papers.title: Vestibular Epilepsy Presenting With Isolated Recurrent Vertigo and Postictal Headache: A Case Report.
papers.summary: A case report of a 38-year-old woman with recurrent brief vertigo and postictal headache, diagnosed with vestibular epilepsy after EEG showed generalized epileptiform discharges and divalproex sodium markedly reduced attack frequency.

papers.title: Success rate of MRI scanning during natural sleep for younger autistic and typically developing toddlers.
papers.summary: In a longitudinal natural-sleep MRI study of 22 autistic and 23 typically developing toddlers, the overall non-sedated scan success rate was 40.3% (36.4% autistic vs 44.1% non-autistic, not significantly different), with 87.5% of failures due to toddlers not falling asleep. Procedural and budgetary differences from higher-success protocols were identified as key considerations.

papers.title: Occupational exposures and cancer risk associated with the practice of urology: A narrative review.
papers.summary: A narrative review of 24 included articles found that urologic surgeons face occupational cancer risk factors including surgical smoke, volatile anesthetic agents, ionizing radiation, chronic stress, sleep deprivation, night work, and prolonged working hours, alongside limited awareness of these risks and inadequate medical follow-up. The authors conclude that improved awareness may support preventive strategies for urologic surgeons.

papers.title: Prevalence and Associations of Depressive and Anxiety Symptoms in Age Related Macular Degeneration and Other Macular Diseases.
papers.journal: Ophthalmic & physiological optics : the journal of the British College of Ophthalmic Opticians (Optometrists)
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional survey of 1364 Australian adults with AMD and other macular diseases, depressive symptoms were present in 15.7% and anxiety in 20.8%, with over half receiving no mental health support. Loneliness, high falls concern, and poor sleep quality were associated with both depressive and anxiety symptoms.

papers.title: Statement of Retraction: Alterations in circadian rhythms aggravate Acetaminophen-induced liver injury in mice by influencing Acetaminophen metabolization and increasing intestinal permeability.
papers.summary: This is a retraction notice for a previously published article on circadian rhythm alterations and acetaminophen-induced liver injury in mice; no abstract or findings are provided.

papers.title: Development of a multidimensional scale for discomfort related to personal protective equipment and its exploratory association with musculoskeletal symptoms among Korean healthcare workers during the COVID-19 pandemic.
papers.journal: Journal of occupational medicine and toxicology (London, England)
papers.summary: In 565 Korean healthcare workers caring for COVID-19 patients, a 17-item PPE Discomfort Scale yielded two factors, direct wearing burden and organisational vulnerability, and musculoskeletal disorder prevalence was 37.2% with lower back most affected. Total PPE discomfort was associated with musculoskeletal symptoms (adjusted PR 1.60), driven by organisational vulnerability rather than direct wearing burden, though associations were attenuated after further adjustment.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
